findings.title: Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the method defined four lines above that takes max_width and max_height. Any existing caller that passes numeric width and height (the previous public signature) now treats the width as the geometry string and the height as `opts`. `opts[:allow_animation]` then raises, and even a rescued failure returns false so thumbnails and other downsizes stop being generated. Keep a single method that accepts either a geometry string or two integers.

findings.title: Downsize reads and writes the same tempfile path
findings.body: The new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`. ImageMagick `convert` cannot reliably use one path as both input and output: it often truncates or replaces the file before the source is fully read, producing an empty or corrupt image. The upload Tempfile is already open, so a convert that writes via a new inode leaves that FD on the original bytes while `tempfile.size` and `Upload.create_for` still use the open file. Downsizing then either no-ops or stores the undownsized (or empty) image. Write to a separate temp path, replace the upload file only after success, and reopen/re-stat before `create_for`.

findings.title: Percentage geometry is invalid for the animated downsize path
findings.body: When the upload is a GIF and `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is on, `optimize` switches to gifsicle instructions (`--resize-fit` plus the dimensions argument). Those instructions expect a WIDTHxHEIGHT, but the new caller passes `"80%"`. gifsicle then fails, `downsize` returns false, and the loop ignores that return value and retries the same file five times. Animated uploads are never reduced and still hit the size check. The non-animated instruction also appends `\>` , so the geometry becomes `80%\>` rather than a plain percentage. Use a WxH target (or a percentage only on the convert path) and stop the loop when downsize returns false.

findings.title: Client size check hardcodes 10MB for every upload type
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` used to read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so images and attachments each followed their site setting. It now always uses `10 * 1024`. Attachments are no longer limited by `max_attachment_size_kb`, and an admin who raised `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB will have the client reject files the server would accept. The 413 handler at the same file was also changed from `max_image_size_kb` to 10MB, so the error text no longer matches the configured or proxy limit. Only relax the client cap for images that the server will downsize, and keep the attachment setting.

findings.title: URL fetches always allow 10MB, including non-images
findings.body: API uploads that pass a URL used to download at most `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. The cap is now a fixed `10.megabytes` for every type, and the later downsize block only runs when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true. Non-image URL uploads therefore bypass the configured size limit and can pull up to 10MB even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is much smaller. Limit the raised cap to images that will actually be downsized, and keep the site setting for other files.

findings.title: No coverage for automatic downsize-on-upload
findings.body: The new upload path (five 80% passes, same-path convert, GIF vs still image, and what happens when the file is still over `max_image_size_kb`) has no tests in this change. A failure of convert, a stale Tempfile size, or an attachment accidentally included in the 10MB cap would ship unnoticed. Add controller or model tests for a still image that shrinks under the setting, a GIF with animation allowed, a downsize that returns false, and a non-image that must still obey the attachment limit.
